name: Income Certificate
eligibility_summary: Any resident of Assam can apply for an Income Certificate, commonly used for scholarships, LPG subsidy, fee concessions, and other welfare schemes. There is no single fixed income threshold to obtain the certificate itself; it records the applicant's or family's declared income. The certificate is issued by the Circle Officer (rural areas) or Sub-Divisional Officer (urban areas) under the Revenue and Disaster Management Department, and is notified as a service under the Assam Right to Public Services (ARTPS) Act, 2012.
required_documents: Address proof and identity proof are required. Salary slip may be required if employed, and land-revenue documentation may be required where applicable, particularly for agricultural income. Applicants should confirm the current checklist for their service variant.
application_steps: Apply online through the Assam Sewa Setu portal (sewasetu.assam.gov.in) by registering, logging in, selecting 'Application for Income Certificate', filling the form, and uploading the required documents. Separate Income Certificate service variants exist for KAAC (Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council) and NCHAC (North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council) areas; residents of those council areas should use the corresponding variant. Applications can also be submitted with assistance at a Public Facilitation Centre (PFC) at the Circle/SDO/DC office, or at a Common Service Centre (CSC). The officially listed online charges are a User/Statutory charge of Rs. 30 and a Convenience fee of Rs. 10; PFC/CSC-assisted applications may involve additional service, printing, or scanning charges as listed on the portal.
estimated_timeline: The listed Assam e-District service timeline is 10 days; actual processing may vary depending on verification and local circumstances. Applicants should treat any specific number of days as approximate and check the current stipulated timeline directly on the portal or with the local Revenue office.

name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
eligibility_summary: Landholding farmer families (husband, wife, and minor children) who own cultivable land as per state/UT land records are eligible for income support. The land is generally required to be recorded in the farmer's name as per applicable land records rules. Certain categories, including institutional landholders and other exclusion categories defined in the scheme guidelines (such as serving/retired government employees above a certain level, income-tax payers, and holders of constitutional posts), are not eligible. Eligible families receive Rs. 6,000 per year in three installments of Rs. 2,000 each via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)
required_documents: Aadhaar card, bank account details for DBT, land ownership/land record documents, and an identity proof such as Voter ID or PAN. The scheme has been moving towards requiring a Farmer ID (linked to the central Farmer Registry / AgriStack initiative) alongside Aadhaar-based e-KYC as part of registration and continued eligibility verification; the specific states and timelines where this is currently mandatory have been changing and are reported inconsistently across sources, so applicants in Assam should verify the current Farmer ID/e-KYC requirement directly on pmkisan.gov.in or with their local agriculture office rather than assume a fixed rule.
application_steps: Register on the official portal pmkisan.gov.in under 'Farmers Corner' > 'New Farmer Registration', choosing Rural or Urban Farmer Registration. Enter Aadhaar number, mobile number, and state, verify via OTP, then fill in personal details, bank details, and land details, and complete Aadhaar-based e-KYC. Registration can also be done via the PM-KISAN mobile app or with assistance at a Common Service Centre (CSC) or local revenue/agriculture office. After submission, the concerned state government verifies the details against land records before approval.
estimated_timeline: Verification and approval time depends on state-level land record verification and is not fixed centrally; applicants should check status on the portal (Farmers Corner > Beneficiary Status) rather than assume a specific number of days.

name: Old Age Pension (Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme)
eligibility_summary: Available to persons aged 60 years or above who belong to a household classified as Below Poverty Line (BPL), under the central Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), Ministry of Rural Development. NSAP is implemented in Assam by the Panchayat & Rural Development (PNRD) Department rather than the Social Welfare Department (as is the case in most other states). Per the official NSAP framework, the central pension amount is Rs. 200 per month for ages 60-79 and Rs. 500 per month from age 80 onward; state governments, including Assam, typically add their own top-up over this central amount, but the exact combined payable amount in Assam can be revised over time and should be confirmed with the local Panchayat or Block office rather than assumed.
required_documents: Documents commonly requested include proof of age, proof of BPL status/BPL list entry, residence proof, and bank or post office account details, along with passport-size photographs. Exact document requirements should be confirmed with the local Gram Panchayat or Block Office, as these are not presented here as a universally fixed mandatory list.
application_steps: Submit the application through the applicable Gaon Panchayat, VCDC, VDC or Block Office under Assam's PNRD process. The application form is commonly made available through PNRD Assam (pnrd.assam.gov.in). After local verification, the application is forwarded for sanction through the applicable district-level process. Application/payment status can be tracked through the NSAP portal (nsap.nic.in).
estimated_timeline: No fixed officially published turnaround time was found for this service; approval depends on local verification and the sanctioning process, so applicants should follow up directly with the Gaon Panchayat or Block Office rather than assume a specific number of days.

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students (Assam)
eligibility_summary: For students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC), permanently resident in Assam, studying in Class XI and above (including diploma, undergraduate, postgraduate, and professional courses) at a recognized institution. This is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme funded by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, and implemented in Assam by the Directorate of Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, Assam. Applicants must meet the annual family-income ceiling specified in the current scheme guidelines; the annual family-income ceiling is Rs. 2.5 lakh under the applicable scheme guidelines. Applicants should verify the exact current ceiling and any category-specific variation for the applicable academic year on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) before applying, as central scholarship income ceilings and amounts can be revised year to year.
required_documents: A valid SC caste certificate (commonly required to be issued by the Office of the District Commissioner/competent authority), an income certificate for parents/guardian (typically issued by the Circle Officer of the relevant Revenue Circle) confirming income is within the applicable ceiling, a Bonafide Certificate from the head of the educational institution, Aadhaar (required to generate the mandatory One Time Registration/OTR number on NSP), and Aadhaar-linked bank account details for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
application_steps: Apply online through the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in / NSP). First complete One Time Registration (OTR) using Aadhaar (via the NSP OTR mobile app and Aadhaar Face RD verification), then select and fill in the Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students application, upload the required documents, and submit before the deadline. The application typically requires subsequent verification by the educational institution and the state Directorate before final approval. The Assam scholarship application window is commonly open for a period during the academic year (recent cycles have opened around June and closed around September, with institute-level verification continuing for some weeks after), but exact dates change annually and must be confirmed on the NSP portal or the Directorate's official notification for the relevant year.
estimated_timeline: No fixed official number of processing days was found; disbursal depends on institute-level verification, state-level Directorate approval, and DBT processing on NSP, so applicants should track their application status using their NSP application ID rather than assume a fixed timeline.

name: Permanent Residence Certificate (PRC)
eligibility_summary: Per the official PRC Guidelines published by the Home & Political Department, Government of Assam, eligibility requires that: the applicant is an Indian citizen; AND either the applicant's parents or forefathers have had permanent residence in Assam for a minimum of 50 years, OR the applicant has personally resided in Assam for a minimum of 20 years. An applicant who satisfies this eligibility may also apply on behalf of their child. Land ownership in Assam is not listed as an independent eligibility route in the official guidelines; it may still appear as a supporting document in some service variants, but is not itself a standalone qualifying condition. The certificate is issued by the Deputy Commissioner of the concerned district. Note that separate PRC service variants exist on the Sewa Setu portal (for example, a variant specifically for Higher Education purposes, and separate variants for NCHAC areas), each with its own exact document checklist, so applicants should select the correct variant for their purpose.
required_documents: Commonly required documents include one address proof of self or parent (such as Aadhaar Card, Voter Card, Ration Card, Electricity Bill, Passport, Bank Passbook, or Driving Licence), documents evidencing the parents'/forefathers' 50-year residence in Assam (or the guardian's 20-year residence, where applicable), a copy of the applicant's birth certificate, and a recent passport-size photograph. Records of immovable property with an up-to-date land revenue (khajna) receipt are commonly requested where applicable. Exact document requirements vary by PRC service variant (general/higher-education/autonomous council areas) and by district, so applicants should check the specific requirements listed for the variant they are applying under on the Sewa Setu portal.
application_steps: Apply online through the Assam Sewa Setu portal (sewasetu.assam.gov.in) by registering/logging in and selecting the relevant Permanent Residence Certificate service (for example, 'Permanent Residence Certificate for Higher Education', or a separate general/council-area variant), filling in the form, and uploading the required documents. Applications can also be made with assistance at a Public Facilitation Centre (PFC) at the Circle Office/SDO Office/DC Office, or at a Common Service Centre (CSC). The certificate is issued after verification by the Deputy Commissioner's office and can be downloaded from the ARTPS portal once approved.
estimated_timeline: For the PRC for Higher Education service, a stipulated timeline of approximately 14 working days has been consistently referenced in relation to the ARTPS/Sewa Setu process; actual processing may vary by district and by which PRC variant is applied for, so applicants should confirm the current stipulated timeline for their specific service on the Sewa Setu portal.

name: Caste Certificate (SC / ST-Plains / ST-Hills / OBC / MOBC)
eligibility_summary: For residents of Assam whose caste/community is recognized as Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe - Plains, Scheduled Tribe - Hills, Other Backward Class (OBC), or More Other Backward Class (MOBC, an Assam state-specific category) under applicable central and/or Assam government lists. Applicants generally need to demonstrate lineage/community status, primarily through the father's existing caste certificate; where that is not available, a recommendation from an authorized caste/tribe/community organization notified by the State Government is used instead. Assam classifies Scheduled Tribes separately into ST(Plains) and ST(Hills), so applicants should select the correct category for their community.
required_documents: Per the official Sewa Setu service listing: Applicant's photograph (Mandatory); proof of date of birth such as Birth Certificate/Aadhaar/PAN/Board Admit Card (Mandatory); proof of residence of the applicant or parent, such as Permanent Resident Certificate/Aadhaar/EPIC/land document/electricity bill/ration card (Mandatory); and the father's caste certificate (Mandatory). A recommendation from an authorized caste/tribe/community organization is required only in cases where the father's caste certificate is not available. Other documents such as the voter list, an affidavit, or an existing caste certificate are Optional. Legacy documents such as NRC 1951 records or historical electoral roll entries are not listed as universally mandatory on the current official checklist and are only relevant in certain individual verification cases, not for every applicant.
application_steps: Apply online through the Sewa Setu portal (sewasetu.assam.gov.in) under 'Issuance of Caste Certificate' (or the applicable SC/ST/OBC/MOBC-specific service), or apply offline/with assistance at a Public Facilitation Centre (PFC) at the Circle Office/SDO Office/DC Office, or at a Common Service Centre (CSC). The relevant nodal department is typically the Department of Welfare of Plain Tribes and Backward Classes, or the Revenue and Disaster Management Department, depending on the category. The application is verified by the Circle Officer or other competent authority before the certificate is issued and made available for download from the ARTPS portal.
estimated_timeline: The officially listed stipulated time limit on the Sewa Setu portal for the Caste Certificate service is 30 working days. Processing may take longer than this if additional local enquiry or verification is required (for example, in cases without a readily available parental caste certificate).

name: Birth Certificate
eligibility_summary: Registration of every birth is mandatory in India under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (as amended by the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023, in force since 1 October 2023), administered nationally by the Registrar General of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, and implemented at the state/local level. A birth must be reported to the concerned Registrar within 21 days of occurrence; in Assam, this is confirmed on the official Sewa Setu portal for domiciliary (home) births. Registration reported after this window is treated as 'delayed registration' with a graded process: if reported after 21 days but within 30 days, late registration applies with the prescribed late fee; if reported after 30 days but within one year, written permission of the Registrar and the prescribed fee are required. if reported after one year, it currently requires an order from a District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, or an Executive Magistrate authorised by the District Magistrate, after verification of correctness and payment of a fee.
required_documents: For a domiciliary (home) birth in Assam, the officially listed documents are: a certificate from the Gaon Burha / Secretary of the Gaon Panchayat / Ward Commissioner / ANM / ASHA worker (with seal and signature) confirming the birth, and identity proof of the father and mother (Aadhaar Card preferred, otherwise PAN/Voter ID/Passport). A parents' marriage certificate is not listed as a required document on the official service page and should not be presented as mandatory. Institutional (hospital) births are typically reported directly by the hospital/institution rather than requiring separate documentary submission by the parents at this stage. Delayed registration cases require additional documents such as a self-attested affidavit or supporting proof, as prescribed by the approving authority.
application_steps: In Assam, birth registration (for domiciliary/home births) can be applied for online through the Sewa Setu portal (sewasetu.assam.gov.in) under 'Birth Registration' (Health and Family Welfare Department), or through the concerned local Registrar of Births & Deaths (such as the municipal corporation/municipal board in urban areas, or the Gaon Panchayat-linked registration unit in rural areas), or with assistance at a Public Facilitation Centre (PFC)/Common Service Centre (CSC). For delayed registration, a separate 'Permission for Delayed Birth Registration' service must be applied for. Nationally, the Civil Registration System (CRS) portal (crsorgi.gov.in) also supports birth registration and provides a central digital record.
estimated_timeline: The officially listed stipulated timeline on the Assam Sewa Setu portal for standard birth registration (within the 21-day window) is 10 days, with the Application Fee listed as NIL for this service. Delayed registration cases take longer, as they depend on the additional approval authority (District Registrar or District/Sub-Divisional/Executive Magistrate) and are not subject to the same 10-day timeline.

name: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)
eligibility_summary: A central scheme under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), Ministry of Rural Development, for widows from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households. The central NSAP framework has used an age band of 40 to 59 years for IGNWPS, while the current Assam PNRD page lists minimum age 40. Applicants should confirm the currently applicable age and transition rules with the local implementing office. The Assam PNRD page currently lists the pension as Rs. 300 per month, increasing to Rs. 500 per month from age 80. In Assam, NSAP (including this scheme) is implemented by the Panchayat & Rural Development (PNRD) Department rather than the Social Welfare Department.
required_documents: Documents commonly requested include proof of widowhood (such as the husband's death certificate), age proof, proof of BPL status/BPL list entry, residence proof, and bank account details, along with passport-size photographs. Exact document requirements should be confirmed with the local Gram Panchayat or Block Office rather than treated as a fixed universal list.
application_steps: Submit the application at the local Gaon Panchayat / VCDC / VDC or Block Office, similar to the process for the old age pension scheme in Assam. Application forms and current guidance are available through PNRD Assam (pnrd.assam.gov.in). After local verification, the application is forwarded through the applicable sanctioning process.
estimated_timeline: No fixed officially published turnaround time was found for this service; processing depends on local verification, so applicants should follow up directly with the Gaon Panchayat or Block Office rather than assume a specific number of days.

name: Indira Miri Universal Widow Pension Scheme
eligibility_summary: A separate Assam state government scheme (distinct from the central IGNWPS), announced in the Assam Budget 2019-20 and formally disbursed to beneficiaries starting in subsequent years, intended to support widows in the state regardless of BPL/APL status ('universal'). The Assam scheme provides support to widows through a one-time immediate family assistance component and a monthly pension component. A 2024 Assam Gazette notification specifies that the one-time assistance covers widows aged 18-45 whose husbands died on or after 1 April 2022. The scheme's original design also provided a monthly pension of Rs. 250 until age 60. Applicants should confirm the currently applicable benefit and eligibility conditions with PNRD because the scheme has been modified through subsequent government notifications.
required_documents: Documents commonly expected include the husband's death certificate, proof of age, residence proof, and bank account details. As with the eligibility criteria, applicants should confirm the exact current document checklist with the local Panchayat or Block Office, since a single authoritative official checklist was not confirmed at the time of this review.
application_steps: Apply through the local Gaon Panchayat / Block Office channels under the Panchayat & Rural Development (PNRD) Department, similar to other PNRD-administered pension schemes in Assam. Applicants should check with PNRD Assam (pnrd.assam.gov.in) or the local Panchayat for the current application process, as a single centralized online application system for this specific scheme was not confirmed at the time of this review.
estimated_timeline: No fixed officially published turnaround time was found for this scheme; applicants should follow up directly with the local Panchayat or Block Office rather than assume a specific number of days.

name: Mukhya Mantrir Nijut Moina Aasoni (Chief Minister's Nijut Moina Scheme)
eligibility_summary: A flagship scheme of the Government of Assam, implemented by the Higher Education Department, providing monthly financial assistance to girl students to promote higher education enrollment, reduce dropout rates, and discourage child marriage. Eligible beneficiaries must be girl students domiciled in Assam, enrolled as regular students in the 1st year of Higher Secondary (Class XI), Graduation (undergraduate), or Post-Graduation / B.Ed. courses at Government, Provincialised, or approved Venture educational institutions in Assam. There is no family income ceiling for this scheme. Students enrolled in private educational institutions are not eligible. Married girls are not eligible at the Higher Secondary and undergraduate levels; however, married girls pursuing Post-Graduation or B.Ed. courses remain eligible. Daughters of serving Ministers, Members of Parliament (MPs), and Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are not eligible. Students who have already received a scooter under the Dr. Banikanta Kakati Merit Award are not eligible unless they opt out of the scooter benefit. In-service candidates admitted to B.Ed. courses on deputation are not eligible. The benefit amount differs by educational level: Rs. 1,000 per month for Higher Secondary students, Rs. 1,250 per month for undergraduate students, and Rs. 2,500 per month for Post-Graduation / B.Ed. students. The financial assistance is provided for 10 months per academic year via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the student's bank account. For continuation in subsequent years, the Head of the Institution typically submits a continuity certificate rather than a fresh application. As scheme guidelines and benefit amounts can be revised by the Government of Assam, applicants should verify the current applicable rules with the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam or their institution.
required_documents: Documents commonly required include Aadhaar card, bank account details (Aadhaar-seeded, for DBT), mark sheet or certificate of the qualifying examination (such as HSLC mark sheet for Higher Secondary, Class XII mark sheet for Graduation, or Graduation mark sheet for Post-Graduation), proof of domicile/residency in Assam, valid mobile number and email ID, and a passport-size photograph. Some institutions may also require SAMARTH portal registration details. Exact document requirements should be confirmed with the student's respective educational institution or the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam, as they may vary by institution and academic year.
application_steps: The application process is conducted offline through the student's educational institution. Eligible students collect the application form from their respective college or university administration, fill the form with personal, academic, and bank account details, attach the required documents, and submit the completed form to the Head of the Institution or the designated Nodal Officer. The institution verifies the student's details and forwards the verified applications to the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam for final approval and DBT processing. Application forms are typically distributed by institutions after an official notification from the Higher Education Department at the start of each academic session. Applicants should check with their institution's administration for the current session's application form availability and submission deadline, as specific dates change each year.
estimated_timeline: No fixed officially published processing timeline was found for this scheme; disbursal depends on institutional verification, Directorate-level approval, and DBT processing. Applicants should follow up with their institution's administration or the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam rather than assume a specific number of days.

name: Mukhya Mantrir Nijut Babu Aasoni (Chief Minister's Nijut Babu Scheme)
eligibility_summary: A scheme of the Government of Assam, implemented by the Higher Education Department, providing monthly financial assistance to male students from economically weaker families to encourage higher education enrollment, improve the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), and reduce dropout rates. Eligible beneficiaries must be male students domiciled in Assam, enrolled as regular students in the 1st year of Undergraduate (UG) or Postgraduate (PG) courses at Government or Provincialised educational institutions in Assam. Unlike the Nijut Moina scheme, this scheme does not cover Higher Secondary (Class XI/XII) students. The annual family income of the applicant must be less than Rs. 4 lakh. Students enrolled in private educational institutions, distance education programmes, or self-financed courses are generally not eligible. Students already receiving benefits under the Dr. Banikanta Kakati Merit Award or the Chief Minister's Jibon Prerana Scheme are not eligible. Beneficiaries are required to maintain regular attendance and adhere to the academic discipline and conduct rules of their institution; failure to do so may result in withdrawal of the benefit. The benefit amount is Rs. 1,000 per month for undergraduate students and Rs. 2,000 per month for postgraduate students, provided for 10 months per academic year via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account. As scheme guidelines and benefit amounts can be revised by the Government of Assam, applicants should verify the current applicable rules with the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam or their institution.
required_documents: Documents commonly required include Aadhaar card, bank account details (must be Aadhaar-seeded, for DBT), an income certificate (or ration card as proof of income) confirming annual family income is below Rs. 4 lakh, mark sheet or certificate of the qualifying examination (such as Class XII mark sheet for Graduation, or Graduation mark sheet for Post-Graduation), proof of domicile/residency in Assam, valid mobile number and email ID, and a passport-size photograph. Exact document requirements should be confirmed with the student's respective educational institution or the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam, as they may vary by institution and academic year.
application_steps: The application process is conducted offline through the student's educational institution. Eligible students collect the application form from their respective college or university administration, fill the form with personal, academic, and bank account details, attach the required documents (including the income certificate), and submit the completed form to the Head of the Institution or the designated Nodal Officer. The institution verifies the student's details and uploads them to the official Directorate of Higher Education (DHE) portal for final approval and DBT processing. Application forms are typically distributed by institutions after an official notification from the Higher Education Department at the start of each academic session. Applicants should check with their institution's administration for the current session's application form availability and submission deadline, as specific dates change each year.
estimated_timeline: No fixed officially published processing timeline was found for this scheme; disbursal depends on institutional verification, Directorate-level approval, and DBT processing. Applicants should follow up with their institution's administration or the Directorate of Higher Education, Assam rather than assume a specific number of days.
